---
title: Change or delete a type
description: Check a change to a registered type, replace its definition, delete a type nothing uses, and remove a platform type a build no longer ships.
---

The examples change the receipt type from [Define a type](/build/define-a-type). Each call sends `receipt.json` as that guide left it, and `definition` is that file read in, as [Register the type](/build/define-a-type#register-the-type) shows. The TypeScript examples use a client made as [the TypeScript SDK](/typescript-sdk) shows, and the Swift examples a `Client` made as [the Swift SDK](/swift-sdk#call-the-server-directly) shows, with `receiptURL` the file's location. [What your key needs](/build/define-a-type#what-your-key-needs) lists the permissions each call takes.

## Change the type

A replacement **sends the whole definition**, so change the file and send all of it. To add an optional category, add `"version": 1` and this field to `receipt.json`:

```json
"category": { "type": "enum", "enum_values": ["travel", "meals", "supplies"] }
```

To check what would change first, normalize the file. Normalizing changes nothing, and any credential can do it, so a connector uses it to decide whether its type needs registering or replacing:

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa types normalize --file receipt.json
```

```http tab="HTTP"
POST /types/normalize
Authorization: Bearer <key>
Content-Type: application/json

<the contents of receipt.json>
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const { data, error } = await marfa.POST("/types/normalize", { body: definition });
```

```swift tab="Swift"
let normalized = try await api.check(itemType: definition)
```

The answer's `type` is your definition with its defaults made explicit, and `registered_type` is the registered one in the same form. Compare those two, not `resolved_type`, which adds what the registered type inherits. Both registered forms are `null` when the identifier isn't registered. An unknown schema key, anywhere in a definition, is refused `400 invalid_schema`.

**A replacement keeps the icon the owner chose** for the type (see [display hints](/catalog/your-own-types#display-hints)), and `registered_type` shows the icon you registered, not the owner's. A `GET` of the type, put back as a replacement, keeps the icon you registered.

Then replace the type:

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa types replace app.example.receipt --file receipt.json
```

```http tab="HTTP"
PUT /types/app.example.receipt
Authorization: Bearer <key>
Content-Type: application/json

<the contents of receipt.json>
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const { data, error } = await marfa.PUT("/types/{id}", {
  params: { path: { id: "app.example.receipt" } },
  body: definition,
});
```

```swift tab="Swift"
let update = try JSONDecoder().decode(
    Components.Schemas.TypeDefinitionUpdate.self, from: Data(contentsOf: receiptURL))
_ = try await api.replace(itemType: "app.example.receipt", with: update)
```

A replacement **changes no item you already hold**. An item meets a property you made required the next time its properties are written. A property you leave out is gone from the type, but items keep their values for it, and a later write isn't refused for them.

Send the `version` every time: a replacement without one sets it back to 0. You can't replace or delete a type Marfa ships.

**A type's identifier never changes.** To rename a type, register the new one, [move the items](/build/move-items-to-another-type) to it, then delete the old one. A move also changes the folders, views and webhooks that name the old type.

## Delete the type

Marfa deletes a type that **no item holds**, in any state and the trash included, that no folder, view or webhook names, and that no other type names as its parent or in `compatible_with`:

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa types delete app.example.receipt
```

```http tab="HTTP"
DELETE /types/app.example.receipt
Authorization: Bearer <key>
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
await marfa.DELETE("/types/{id}", {
  params: { path: { id: "app.example.receipt" } },
});
```

```swift tab="Swift"
try await api.delete(itemType: "app.example.receipt")
```

Otherwise it refuses with `409 type_in_use` when items hold the type or a setting names it, `409 type_has_subtypes` when a type names it as its parent, and `422 compatible_with_violation` when a type names it in `compatible_with`.

A `type_in_use` refusal counts the items in `details.item_count` and names each folder, view and webhook setting in `details.settings`, without the `id` of a setting your key can't read. **[Move the items to another type](/build/move-items-to-another-type) first:** the move changes those settings too. `details.grants` lists the keys and apps whose type map names the type, if your key may manage them. They don't stop a delete, so change them through [Manage keys](/run/manage-keys) when you're ready.

<Callout type="warn" title="A forced delete blocks writes to the items">
A key can send `force=true` (the CLI's `--force`) to delete a type that items still hold or a setting names. A subtype or a `compatible_with` claim still blocks it. The items and settings stay, but Marfa refuses writes to the items' properties, tier or time until the type is registered again. You can still tag, archive or trash them.
</Callout>

The owner can remove an unused type without a key: with a [sign-in from the last five minutes](/run/sign-in-as-the-owner#confirm-its-you), select **Remove type** on the type's page under **Items** in the owner's console, or send the deletion through the private socket. Marfa makes the same checks, and refuses `force=true` from the owner with `403 forbidden`.

## Remove a retired platform type

A build can stop shipping a type that an earlier build shipped. An instance that held it keeps the type as a **retired platform type**, and it stays in `GET /types` until you remove it. `GET /health` counts them as `platform_types.retired`.

[List retired platform types](/api-reference/health-and-maintenance/listRetiredPlatformTypes), or `marfa types retired`, answers each one with how many items carry it, the types that name it as their parent, and `removable`. It needs the `instance.read` permission.

[Delete a retired platform type](/api-reference/health-and-maintenance/deleteRetiredPlatformType), or `marfa types delete-retired <id>`, removes one whose `removable` is `true`: no item carries it, and no type inherits from it or names it in `compatible_with`. It needs `instance.maintain`.
